images.filename: Belfast City Council Seat Share by Year 1973-2023.png
images.caption:
Share of seats to unionist nationalist or other/cross-community parties in the Belfast City Council from 1973 to 2019. Alliance councillors are counted as other in all years.
Unionist seat share is shown in blue with triangular markers. This line has generally been trending downwards, at a fairly constant rate, since 1973 where it started at 67%. It went below 50% in 1997, and is currently the second largest group at 28%.
Nationalist seat share is shown in green with circular markers. This line was increasing fairly consistently from 1973, where it started at 18%, until reaching 45% in 2001, where it has since plateaued. It's higest share has been 47% in 2011, and is currently the largest group on 46.6%.

The other/cross-community seat share is shown in green with square markers. This line was in a fairly steady plateau below 16% since 1973, until it has increased rapidly in recent elections, reaching 25% in 2023, making it the third largest group. There was one exception to this graph in 1977, where it gained 27% of the seats, before falling back below 16% for the rest of the century.

images.caption: Bedford Street, Belfast (2). See 761951.   The view along Bedford Street, from the City Hall end, towards the Dublin Road.  The "Causeway Exchange" is on the right - originally a 70's monstrosity (and called "Griffin House"), clad in dingy concrete panels but nicely re-clad, in red brick, a few years ago.  Very quiet on a Sunday morning but can be a bit hectic during the evening peak.

images.caption: CS Lewis streets, Belfast 317441 gives some indication of CS Lewis's connection with east Belfast.  The redevelopment of the area off Severn Street (bottom left) saw three new streets named in his memory.  They are (right and working back) Lewis Park, Lewis Avenue and Lewis Drive.  For the information of ex-pats, the houses are to the south east of Yukon Street.  Continue to 1378885.

images.caption:
Chimneys, Belfast. The BBC has expanded far beyond the original Broadcasting House 564271 (known - I'm told - as "BH") and needs more heat than ever.  This is the view from Linenhall Street.  It might be an interesting experience to capture the hot air generated by callers to Messrs Nolan and Dunseith and use it to reduce the Beeb's heating bill - just a thought . . . . 
For the record part of the extension was built on the site of an old warehouse at 55 Linenhall Street.
